bib.title: Bi-Mamba: Towards Accurate 1-Bit State Space Models

read.skipped: References skimmed; weight-distribution histogram figures (Figs 7-10) not interpretable from text

question: Can Mamba-2 state space models be binarized to 1-bit weights and trained from scratch while keeping performance close to full precision?
hypothesis: Binarization-aware training with autoregressive distillation preserves Mamba quality where post-training quantization and binarization fail.
contributions: First work to binarize the Mamba architecture to 1-bit from scratch while maintaining strong performance
Explore the parameter space for binarization in Mamba
Pretrained Bi-Mamba usable as a base model for resource-limited downstream tasks

method.summary: Replaces the input and output projection linears of Mamba-2 (780M, 1.3B, 2.7B) with FBI-Linear (sign weights in {1,-1} with learnable column-wise scale alpha and shift beta), trained with STE and a cross-entropy distillation loss from a LLaMA2-7B teacher on 105B Amber tokens. Embedding/head, conv1d, A, D, norm and delta_bias stay at 16 bits.
method.task: language-model pretraining via binarization-aware autoregressive distillation

limits: Weights are simulated with high-precision values in accuracy experiments; real 1-bit packing is only evaluated on CPU via llama.cpp (Table 8) and storage is theoretical (Table 7)
Authors concede possible accuracy trade-offs on complex tasks and that specialized hardware is needed to maximize gains
Training from scratch with distillation is compute-intensive (4640-7822 A100 hours)
Mamba base models are weak on HumanEval and GSM8K (near zero) so those comparisons are uninformative
1-bit models still trail FP16 Mamba-2 on average accuracy by about 7-9 points; 2.7B downstream is comparable to OneBit
No training seeds, no sequence length or context length stated; text 'until convergence' conflicts with appendix
Only tested on Mamba-2; BitNet comparison not matched in size (700M, 3B)
